title: njutest assurance report v1
description: One durable assurance document: an envelope naming whether it is a whole-catalog answer or one deliberately partial shard, and beneath that tag what was asked, what ran, what it established, and every limitation on the claim. There is no percentage in this document, by design — a verdict is a claim a reader can check, and a coverage number is not.

document_type.description: Whether the report beneath is a whole-catalog answer, or one part of a divided catalog that assures nothing on its own and exists only to be merged.

allOf.description: The tag names which document is under it; a complete answer under a shard tag, or the reverse, is not a document this schema reads.

opaque.description: A SHA-256 in lower-case hex, or the sentinel "unavailable".

runId.description: A canonical run identity, which is also its directory name under reports/runs.

provenance.description: Where the facts in this report came from. A run that read an earlier run's answer says so and names it, so a reader can check the claim rather than take it.

identity.description: The evidence identity of the inputs, which is what a cached answer is keyed on.

source_run_id.description: The run that established the facts, present exactly when cached is true.

allOf.description: A report read back from an earlier run names it, and one this run established names nobody. Neither of the other combinations is a document this schema accepts.

git.description: Either git could be asked and every field says what it said, or it could not and every field is the explicit unavailable state — never an empty string, which would read as "nothing to say".

allOf.description: A tree git could not be asked about carries none of the facts only git could have said, and a list of files that differ from a base names the base. Neither half of either pair is a document this schema accepts without the other, because a reader meeting one cannot tell which half to believe.
A base and the files taken against it travel together: either alone is half a fact.

configured_builds.description: The configured builds the request required, in configuration order. The retained build ledger names this exact sequence.

targets.description: Every selected target has exactly one terminal state, so passed + failed + skipped + missing equals selected.

mutants.description: reused_killed and reused_survived are parts of killed and survived, not additions to them.

observers.description: Who decided each catalogued mutation. These partition the catalog; the counts beside them overlap.

executed.description: False under standard-v1, where the phase is a static inventory and a non-empty one is a limitation.

candidates.description: Every repair a generation provider offered, and what putting it to the tests established. A candidate is a proposal: nothing here has been written into the tree.

resources.description: Every integration resource the run held while its tests ran, in the order it started them. A resource is a fact about the world the tests ran in, so a run that held none says so with an empty list.

environment.description: The variable names the provider set for every test process, in name order. Never a value: a report is read by people who may not hold the secret in it.

seams.description: Every question licensed by a watched seam recording, with its closed answer.

status.description: A target that could not be found is missing, which is fail-closed rather than a pass.

mutant.description: One mutation with nested, closed decision and reuse provenance.

catalog_index.description: The dense zero-based position in the canonical catalog, which is what shard membership is a function of.

accepted.description: Whether a reviewer explicitly accepted this surviving, unreached, or equivalent mutation.

findingOrigin.description: Which configured-build evidence raised a finding.

oneOf.description: A configuration or catalog fact not produced by executing one build.

build.description: The exact name in the document's builds.

oneOf.description: Evidence produced by one retained source namespace for one configured build and catalog part.

position.description: Two 1-based columns, because one toolchain uses two units: an llvm-cov region counts UTF-8 bytes and a rustc diagnostic counts Unicode scalars. Both come from one byte offset, so they cannot disagree.

gained.description: Catalog indices only the control reported.

lost.description: Catalog indices only the baseline reported.

drift.description: What a run established about whether one measured target's baseline reach holds.

catalogPart.description: The part of a catalog one evidence source measured: the whole catalog, or one valid `index/of` shard.

shardPart.description: A valid `index/of` shard identity, where index is at most of.

composition.description: How this complete response was assembled.

oneOf.description: One whole-catalog configured run completed directly.

sources.description: Every partial input, in canonical shard order.

oneOf.description: A complete set of partial report envelopes was merged.

mergeSource.description: One partial report envelope consumed by a complete shard merge.

buildSelection.description: The exact Cargo inputs for one configured build, with the domain-separated canonical digest of the other seven fields.

features.description: Strictly sorted and duplicate-free, which the digest is derived from.

source.description: One file a source's mutants were read from, and its SHA-256 as the source read it.

path.description: The file, from the workspace root.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes.

buildPartEvidence.description: Every fact established by one source run for one configured build and one whole catalog or shard.

run_id.description: The canonical run namespace that owns these facts.

targets.description: The baseline target facts, in canonical target order.

sources.description: The SHA-256 of each file this source's mutants were read from, as it read them, one entry per file in path order; a reader holds a file to it before drawing any line of it as the code the run measured.

drift.description: Whether each target this source's baseline measured reached, on an original-code control over the same passing tests, what it reached on that baseline (ADR 0025).

buildEvidence.description: Every source of truth for one configured build.

name.description: The configuration name (`default` for the primary build).

parts.description: The complete evidence-source ledger: exactly one whole-catalog source, or every shard of one denominator in index order.

shardBuildEvidence.description: One configured build's evidence for a single catalog shard.

name.description: The configuration name (`default` for the primary build).

source.description: The one source namespace that measured this shard.

modelCompletion.description: The model-phase state of a durable complete report. There is no pending state: either the contract has no model phase, or its exact survivor set has been answered.

oneOf.description: `standard-v1` or `deep-v1`; no model answer is meaningful.
`verified-v1`; every post-lattice survivor has one retained answer.

modelBatch.description: One final-run-owned, catalog-ordered model answer batch.

owner.description: The final report namespace, not any per-build source namespace.

records.description: Every verified-v1 eligibility or verifier answer, keyed by full mutation identity.

completeReport.description: A whole-catalog answer. The non-empty build ledger is the sole source of execution evidence; verdicts, counters, and row projections are derived from it and never stored.

run_kind.description: How much of the workspace the run looked at. It bounds which verdicts the run may reach.

tool.description: Producer versions shared by every build.

repository.description: Repository evidence shared by every build.

scope.description: The exact requested scope and configured build order.

builds.description: The sole source of execution evidence, in configuration order with the default build first.

global_findings.description: Run-wide findings derived without executing any one build, retained exactly once rather than copied into each source.

model_completion.description: The terminal contract-specific model state produced after the cross-build and cross-shard lattice.

shardReport.description: One deliberately partial `K/N` document. It cannot be passed where a completed answer is required; only shard merge consumes it.

run_kind.description: How much of the workspace the run looked at. It bounds which verdicts the run may reach.

tool.description: Producer versions shared by every build.

repository.description: Repository evidence shared by every build.

allOf.description: A shard document carries its part as the typed field beside the ledger, not as scope text.

shard.description: The one part of the catalog this document measured.

builds.description: The non-empty configured-build ledger, every source of which measured this same shard.

global_findings.description: Run-wide findings derived without executing any one build, retained exactly once rather than copied into each source.
